source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Adopt the change permanently without collecting outcome data because a published intervention does not need local evaluation after implementation.","B":"Reject the change unless every staff member already agrees with it because quality-improvement work should not proceed when practice variation exists.","C":"Use current evidence within the organized improvement process, help implement or test the change appropriately, and evaluate its effect on client outcomes.","D":"Keep the existing process unchanged until a serious pressure injury occurs because preventive quality improvement is not part of entry-level RN practice."}}
source_row.rationale: NCSBN's current Management of Care blueprint includes using research for performance-improvement actions, participating in QI processes, and evaluating their impact. Option C integrates all three expectations. Option A omits evaluation, Option B makes unanimous preexisting agreement a false prerequisite, and Option D incorrectly excludes preventive improvement from RN practice.

source_row.stem: A unit is considering an evidence-based change to its pressure-injury prevention process. Which nursing action is most consistent with the NCLEX Management of Care quality-improvement role?
